# multimod [<img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="130" alt="multimod website" />](https://optimal2050.github.io/multimod/)

> **One optimization model, many representations.**

**multimod** is an R toolkit for defining, translating, documenting, and
solving algebraic optimization models. It stores a model as a common abstract
syntax tree (AST), separating the mathematical structure from any one modeling
language or solver interface.

From that shared representation, multimod can:

- inspect, validate, visualize, fold, trim, and serialize a model;
- render equations or a complete formulation as LaTeX;
- generate GAMS, GMPL/MathProg, Julia/JuMP, Python/Pyomo, or R code; or
- bypass generated model code and assemble a solver-ready LP matrix directly,
  write MPS, or solve in-process with HiGHS.

The package grew from energy-system modeling, but the AST and rendering
machinery are domain-independent.

## Why a common model representation?

Mathematical models often become coupled to the language in which they were
first written. multimod separates three concerns:

1. **Model meaning** — sets, parameters, variables, mappings, equations, and
   objectives in the AST.
2. **Representation** — human-readable LaTeX, executable backend code, JSON,
   or a sparse LP/MPS matrix.
3. **Execution** — a local solver, an institutional modeling environment, or
   remote hardware.

That separation makes it possible to compare backends, document the exact
model being solved, manipulate it before execution, and reuse one formulation
across several solver ecosystems.

## Architecture

``` text
┌─────────────────────────────┐
│      Input Formats          │
├─────────────────────────────┤
│ GAMS    (basic/linear only) │ → read_gams()
│ GMPL    (limited features)  │ → read_gmpl()
│ {JuMP}  (planned)           │ → {read_jump()}
│ {Pyomo} (planned)           │ → {read_pyomo()}
│ {{AMPL, MPS, ...}}          │ → {{...}}
└─────────────────────────────┘
              ↓
   ┌────────────────────────┐
   │   multimod Core        │        Analysis & Manipulation:
   │ (Abstract Syntax Tree) │         • fold_model()        [✓]
   ├────────────────────────┤         • trim_model()        [✓]
   │ • Sets & Aliases       │  →      • save_model()        [✓]
   │ • Parameters           │         • as_visNetwork()     [✓]
   │ • Variables            │  ←      • model statistics    [✓]
   │ • Equations            │         • model_to_json()     [✓]
   │ • Mappings             │         {{auto-mapping}}      [ ]
   └────────────────────────┘         {{symbolic simplify}} [ ]
                 ↓                                     ↓
┌──────────────────────────────────┐  ┌──────────────────────────────────┐
│ Output: model code               │  │ Output: LP matrix                │
├──────────────────────────────────┤  ├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ LaTeX    write_latex()       [✓] │  │ model_to_lp()               [✓]  │
│ GMPL     write_gmpl()        [✓] │  │ write_mps()                 [✓]  │
│ JuMP     write_jump()        [✓] │  │ solve_highs()               [✓]  │
│ Pyomo    write_pyomo()       [✓] │  │ solve_mps()                 [✓]  │
│ GAMS     write_gams() +      [✓] │  │ read_mps_solution()         [✓]  │
│          write_gams_data()       │  │                                  │
│ {{AMPL, ...}}                [ ] │  │ no generated model text, so      │
│                                  │  │ no model-build step — the        │
│ then an external solver:         │  │ time and memory wall on          │
│ glpsol, Julia, Python, NEOS      │  │ large models                     │
└──────────────────────────────────┘  └──────────────────────────────────┘

Status: [✓] implemented | [~] and { } developing | [ ] and {{ }} considering
```

### Current capability

| Direction | Implemented |
|---|---|
| Define | R constructors and DSL for declarations, references, expressions, and equations |
| Read | GAMS models (partial language coverage); GMPL models and data (limited coverage) |
| Inspect and transform | AST validation, model statistics, visualization, `fold_model()`, `trim_model()` |
| Document | Equation and full-model LaTeX rendering |
| Generate code | GAMS, GMPL/MathProg, JuMP, Pyomo, and plain R |
| Interchange and storage | JSON AST serialization; Arrow IPC, Parquet, and CSV model workspaces with lazy data loading |
| Build matrices | Sparse LP arrays, MPS output, coefficient diagnostics |
| Solve | In-process HiGHS, written MPS, or generated backend code |

Reader and writer coverage are intentionally reported separately. multimod can
write languages that it cannot yet read, and parsing a source language does not
imply support for every feature of that language.

## Installation

Install the development version from GitHub:

``` r
pak::pkg_install("optimal2050/multimod")
```

Backend runtimes are optional. Install only the solver or language toolchains
needed for the routes you intend to use.

## Quickstart

The package includes an energyRt-derived example model:

``` r
library(multimod)

mod <- example_models$energyRt$multimod
class(mod)
#> [1] "model"    "multimod"

eq <- mod$equations[["eqObjective"]]
print(eq)
```

Render the same equation in mathematical notation or executable languages:

``` r
as_latex(eq) |> cat()
as_gams(eq)  |> cat()
as_jump(eq)  |> cat()
```

Or inspect its expression tree:

``` r
as_visNetwork(eq)
```

To parse an existing source model instead:

``` r
mod <- read_gams("model.gms")
# or
mod <- read_gmpl("model.mod", data_file = "model.dat")
```

## Document or translate a complete model

Produce a mathematical appendix directly from the model:

``` r
write_latex(
  mod,
  file = "model-equations.tex",
  title = "Model equations"
)
```

Generate code for another modeling environment:

``` r
save_model(mod, "model-workspace", format = "ipc")

write_gams(mod,  file = "model.gms")
write_gmpl(mod,  model_dir = "model-workspace")
write_jump(mod,  model_dir = "model-workspace")
write_pyomo(mod, model_dir = "model-workspace")
```

The generated code can then be executed with the corresponding local or remote
runtime.

## Skip code generation: build the LP directly

For a linear model, multimod can evaluate the AST into sparse solver arrays
without asking GAMS, JuMP, Pyomo, or GMPL to rebuild the symbolic model:

``` r
lp <- model_to_lp(mod)
check_matrix_numbers(lp)

result <- solve_highs(mod, lp = lp)

# Or write a portable solver input:
write_mps(mod, "model.mps", lp = lp)
```

This route avoids the symbolic build step that can dominate time and memory on
large models. `solve_mps()` provides the local file round trip; solution
readers support HiGHS and cuOpt formats.

## energyRt and cloud solving

[energyRt](https://github.com/optimal2050/energyRt) uses multimod as a model
compiler and interchange layer:

``` text
energyRt scenario
      |
      v
multimod AST --> LaTeX / backend code
      |
      v
   LP / MPS --> local solver
      |
      +------> mmcloud --> cloud CPU/GPU solver --> solution
```

With energyRt loaded, `multimod::as_multimod(scen)` builds the AST from an
interpolated scenario. `mmcloud` can
then transport an MPS file and solver command to cloud hardware and return the
solution; multimod remains responsible for the mathematical model and matrix.

## Development status

multimod is experimental. APIs and supported language subsets may change, and
cross-backend output should be validated for the model features you use.

See the [Get started](https://optimal2050.github.io/multimod/articles/multimod.html)
article for the AST and DSL, the
[development status](https://optimal2050.github.io/multimod/articles/devstatus.html)
for backend coverage, and the
[roadmap](https://optimal2050.github.io/multimod/articles/roadmap.html) for
planned readers and transformations.
